claims.statement: The Go port is module github.com/varveio/swath/go, command go/cmd/swath, with CLI name swath; upstream says it replaces the Java tool at release, and until then the Java release keeps a different launcher and output contract, so the two are separate tools here.
claims.qualification: Stated by the port's own README at the pinned revision. The two share a repository, a name and a dataset family but not a command line (flags were renamed without aliases), and the output format differs (a SeekParquet dataset, which a Java reader does not read).

claims.statement: The subject is commit 8c8f870801c700f22413581f35683096782329a0 on upstream's main, read on 2026-11-11; it is not a release. The port's first release candidate, v0.4.0-rc.1 (a GitHub pre-release of 2026-11-10 with binaries and images), was tagged on an ancestor of the pin, 29 commits earlier; the capsule does not select it.
claims.qualification: Read from the public repository and its releases page on 2026-11-11. The README at the pin still says the Go implementation is unreleased on main and that the latest published release is Java v0.3.2; the pre-release is a candidate, not a release. The capsule was pinned to a2efe16e45d66088f6447e9723a119e5aebd4a91 (the merge of varveio/swath#255) before this commit, and to that pull request's head, 7b05605444766de4e7a736db0bc410409af47429, before that; research/derivation.md lists what moved. Each anchor names the full commit.

claims.statement: The port builds as one pure-Go static binary with CGO_ENABLED=0 through go/build.sh; upstream CI cross-builds it, and the replay server, that way for linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64 and windows/amd64.
claims.qualification: Upstream CI builds each target and runs only the linux/amd64 binaries' --version. go.mod states go 1.26.0, the minimum, and toolchain go1.27.4, the release upstream's CI and images compile with; build/Dockerfile compiles with that toolchain.

claims.statement: The port reports the version and revision set at link time with -X github.com/varveio/swath/go/internal/buildinfo.Version and .Revision, falling back to devel and to Go's VCS build info when none was set; build/Dockerfile passes no version and the pinned commit, so --version prints swath devel (<commit>) and the run report's build names tool swath, version devel and that revision.
claims.qualification: An archive carries no git metadata, so the revision is passed in rather than read, as upstream CI does through SWATH_REVISION; the version stays unset, as it is for any build but a release. The report's build.tool is swath, no longer swath-go as at the capsule's earlier pins. The stamp is a build input, not an independent check that the archive is that commit; the checksum-pinned archive in build/image.json is the identity.

claims.statement: An S3 listing is a tree of key ranges: a provider expands a range into rows that are already ascending plus child ranges that sort between them, and the order stage walks that tree depth-first, so rows reach the writer in global key order with no external sort and no merge pass.
claims.qualification: Established from the port's architecture page at the pinned revision; no run instruments the range tree. Splits are made by the range's owner when workers are idle, not stolen, unlike the Java engine's work-stealing scan. Rows ahead of the frontier may spill to disk and be read back in key order.

claims.statement: --workers defaults to 64 for S3 whatever the CPU count, has no upper bound, and sets both the listing workers and the maximum of the adaptive request limiter, whose limit starts at that maximum.
claims.qualification: The flag refuses a count below 1; unset, the configuration takes the provider's default, and S3 states none, so DefaultWorkers applies. The client builds its limiter at the worker count, and NewLimiter starts its limit at its maximum. This is why the capsule declares concurrency as a Ceiling of 64 rather than a Default: with the limiter on the achieved width is lower and data-dependent. Unlike the Java engine, which starts at min(4, N), the port starts at N unless the diagnostic --adaptive-limit-slow-start is given.

claims.statement: With the adaptive limit on, the default, the limit is multiplied by 0.7 when a throttle answer arrives while at least 15 % of a sliding window of answers (4 per worker, 256 to 4096) are throttles, and grows by one permit per second while the window holds under 7.5 % throttles or after 10 seconds without one; --no-adaptive-limit removes the limiter, so the --workers listing workers run with seed listings and structure probes beside them and nothing bounds the requests in flight to --workers.
claims.qualification: Constants and defaults read from source; growth also freezes while successful attempts are slow or attempts time out. The rule changed from the capsule's earlier pin, where every throttle answer cut the limit and --limiter=false kept a fixed --workers in flight. No run has exercised the limiter against real throttling, so how far below the ceiling a run settles is unknown.

claims.statement: The seed, on by default, tiles the scope from delimiter listings of the folder hierarchy before any range lists, within a delimiter budget of 64 requests and 6 round trips, and stops following a level's pages once a page holds no folder; its first wave also sends the scope's first data page, outside that budget: an untruncated page is the whole listing and no tiles are made, a truncated one is discarded at one request more. The switch that turns the seed off, --no-seed, is a diagnostic flag registered only on swath diag list.
claims.qualification: Read from the flag registration, the policy and the range-engine page. It changes the request pattern, not the output. The first-page shortcut (SeedFirstPage, set with the seed) and the stop on folderless pages are absent at the capsule's earlier pin, so startup and request counts differ from runs at that pin, flat fixtures included. The capsule exposes it as the seed config key: false runs swath diag list --no-seed, and true renders nothing, since swath list has no seed switch at this pin and always seeds.

claims.statement: --structure=auto|on|off, the structure probes a split pivots on, is registered only on swath diag list; swath list runs at its default, auto.
claims.qualification: Read from the flag registration. A case that states structure therefore runs swath diag list, which takes every list flag plus the diagnostic ones; upstream says the diagnostic options exist to run an experiment or a comparison, not to operate the tool, and swath list refuses them.

claims.statement: The S3 flags are --s3-region, --s3-profile, --s3-requester-pays, --s3-path-style and --no-s3-path-style, the --s3-bearer-token flags, --s3-fips, --s3-dualstack and --s3-fetch-owner, beside the object-store flags --endpoint-url, --anonymous, --request-timeout, --ca-bundle and --no-verify-ssl; --anonymous sends no credentials whatever is configured, and a custom endpoint is addressed path-style unless --no-s3-path-style.
claims.qualification: Read from the flag registration. The capsule's earlier pins spelled these --region, --endpoint and --path-style; the old spellings are not aliases at this pin, only names the unknown-flag error suggests the new flag for. Without --anonymous the AWS SDK default chain applies. --endpoint-url defaults to AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3, else AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, so an environment that sets either redirects an unstated endpoint. The capsule renders --endpoint-url only for replay, which matches the Java capsule's --endpoint-url with its path-style default; the replay endpoint is plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1.

claims.statement: With a directory -o, swath list writes a globally key-sorted swath dataset: dense, disjoint data/part-NNNNN.parquet parts and a SeekParquet manifest.json (format seekparquet, format_version 0, draft_revision 1) listing them in order with exact base64 key bounds, row counts, sizes and sha256 digests, with the source, scope and coverage under extensions.swath.
claims.qualification: This replaces the swath-dataset format 2 of the capsule's earlier pins, whose manifest held source, scope and coverage at the top level and an md5 per part. Neither is the Java format 1: there is no _SUCCESS or symlink.txt. The capsule's normalizer reads the parts in manifest order and checks rows and sizes against the manifest; it does not check digests or key bounds.

claims.statement: manifest.json is installed last by an atomic rename and a directory sync; without it there is no dataset, even though a journaled run publishes parts into data/ before the end.
claims.qualification: Stated by the port's output documentation. It is why the normalizer refuses a directory with no manifest rather than reading whatever parts are present.

claims.statement: The manifest's extensions.swath coverage states whether the dataset is its whole scope: complete, stop_reason, skipped_entries and filters, with scope whole or prefix; upstream says a listing with complete true, stop_reason completed, no skipped entries and no filters covers its whole scope minus its exclusions, and leaves what an absent member means to the application.
claims.qualification: This is the tool's own statement of completeness, not a verification of it. Upstream no longer prescribes a refusal for a missing member, as it did at the capsule's earlier pin; the normalizer still refuses one, and requires a scope equal to the case's prefix.

claims.statement: The S3 schema swath/s3-objects/v1 has nine columns, key, size, last_modified, etag, storage_class, owner_id, owner_display_name, checksum_algorithm and checksum_type, with key a STRING-annotated byte array, unique, and last_modified a UTC microsecond timestamp.
claims.qualification: Every row is a current object; the Java schema's version_id, is_latest, is_delete_marker and row_type are not stored (they are in swath/s3-versions/v1, which --all-versions writes and the capsule does not render). Owner columns are null unless --s3-fetch-owner. ETags lose one pair of surrounding quotes in the dataset.

claims.statement: A -o name ending .tsv, optionally .gz or .zst, makes swath list write one TSV file, not a dataset: a header of the S3 schema's column names in the schema's order (key, size, last_modified, etag, storage_class, owner_id, owner_display_name, checksum_algorithm, checksum_type) and one row per object with the dataset's values, the ETag without its quotes and every time in UTC with six fraction digits and Z.
claims.qualification: Read from the writer and the output page. This replaces the S3-API-shaped file of the capsule's earlier pins (Key, LastModified, ETag ... with the ETag quoted and +00:00 times). The file is written to a temporary beside the destination and renamed only when complete. The Java capsule's recursive-tsv-zstd wrote a directory of text parts; the port has none, so the two capsules' products of that mode differ in shape.

claims.statement: In the TSV file every field is written in one escape grammar: \\ a backslash, \t, \n and \r those bytes, \xHH (two lowercase hex digits) any other byte below 0x20, DEL and any byte not part of valid UTF-8; a field that is exactly \N is null. It is reversible and keeps a row on one line.
claims.qualification: Read from the writer and the output page. This replaces the JSON string escapes of the capsule's earlier pins (\b, \f, \u00xx). The normalizer reverses exactly these escapes and refuses any other backslash sequence; a key that unescapes to a tab, LF or CR is refused at the contract's emit boundary, as for every tool.

claims.statement: A text run keeps no journal: swath resume refuses a text destination, and an interrupted text run is run again.
claims.qualification: From the writer and the command pages. Only the dataset mode has a resume mode in this capsule. A text file's spill goes to a scratch directory beside the file, .NAME.swath-ATTEMPT-RANDOM/spill/, on the output's filesystem, where the capsule's earlier pins spilled to the process's temporary directory.

claims.statement: --sort-buffer bounds the bytes of rows and scheduler metadata held between listing and encoding, not resident memory; it defaults to 1/16 of the least of physical memory, the cgroup's limit and GOMEMLIMIT, at most 1 GiB (128 MiB when none is found), and refuses less than 128 KiB. When it is full, rows of ranges ahead of the frontier spill to disk, capped by --spill-budget (0, the default: half the free space on the spill filesystem at start, after a reserve).
claims.qualification: Read from the flags and the limits. The capsule's earlier pins named these --row-budget (a fixed 128 MiB default) and --spill-max; a journal that recorded --row-budget resumes under --sort-buffer. The default now follows the box: a subject container capped at 8 GiB gets 512 MiB, one capped at 16 GiB or an uncapped 64 GiB box 1 GiB (so four swath-go replay plans run at 512 MiB, idc-open-data, noaa-nws-fourcastnetgfs-pds and the live plans at 1 GiB), where the earlier pins' runs had 128 MiB. The capsule exposes both as sort_buffer and spill_budget. Peak memory and spill at scale are run questions.

claims.statement: --encoders N sets the Parquet encoders, a .zst file's compression jobs and a TSV file's row formatters; unset, the port takes the least of GOMAXPROCS and what the sort buffer admits, and may raise a Parquet run's maximum after listing, while an explicit count is kept as the maximum. It is accepted on list, diag list and resume, and a count below 1 is refused.
claims.qualification: Read from the flag table and the limits at the pin. The capsule exposes it as encoders, rendered on every mode including resume. GOMAXPROCS follows the subject container's cpuset, so the automatic count moves with the CPUs a row gives the subject. What a stated count does to wall and memory is a run question.

claims.statement: The pin has no profiling flag: SWATH_CPUPROFILE=FILE (and SWATH_MEMPROFILE=FILE) make the command write a Go pprof CPU (allocation) profile. The path is checked as --report's is, the CPU profile starts before the listing runs and stops when listing.Run returns, before the outcome is classified and the report is written.
claims.qualification: Read from the command and its help at the pin; upstream calls it a development hook. The capsule's cpu_profile: on sets SWATH_CPUPROFILE to swath-go-cpu.pprof at the sink's top level, which the harness keeps on every attempt up to its size bound. The profiler's cost on a run's wall is unmeasured, so a profiled row is diagnostic.

claims.statement: --report FILE writes the JSON run report, with the outcome and a random attempt id, to FILE when the attempt ends, on failure too, though not for a command line that does not parse; FILE may not be a directory, the text output file or one of the dataset directory's own entries.
claims.qualification: Read from the flag and the run-report page. A process killed hard writes no report, and the resume step reuses the list step's path, so the killed step's report must be copied out before the resume runs. The report's invocation.argv is the command in its canonical spelling (--name=value, operands last), not the argv as given. The harness keeps the file on every attempt because RUN_REPORT_NAMES lists swath-go-report.json.

claims.statement: swath resume DIR continues an interrupted object-store dataset run from the journal in DIR/.swath/ with the command it recorded; only runtime and operational flags may be given again, a recorded switch is undone by its other spelling (--no-anonymous, --adaptive-limit), and on a complete dataset it exits 0 with nothing to do.
claims.qualification: The flag sets are read from source and the behaviour from the command page. The source, route, filters, schema and part size are fixed for the run, so a resume that resolves another route is refused. The capsule's resume step restates the case's runtime and operational settings that a resume accepts (workers, the signing choice, adaptive limit, sort buffer, spill budget, deadline, part interval) and refuses the seed, structure and part size, which are frozen.

claims.statement: The exit code classifies the outcome: 0 completed, 1 fatal or incomplete, 2 usage or refused, 74 disk full, 75 stuck, 124 deadline, 130 interrupted, 143 terminated; 74, 75, 124, 130 and 143 leave a journaled run resumable.
claims.qualification: From the exit-codes reference. A dataset committed with partial coverage exits 1, so a partial dataset never exits 0.

claims.statement: --max-duration defaults to 0, no limit, and upstream says to give every unattended run one, with the supervisor's own kill deadline above --max-duration plus 20 seconds.
claims.qualification: The capsule cannot see the harness's timeout, so max_duration is a plan-stated config key; the plans in benchmark/plans/campaigns/swath-go-* state it 30 seconds below the row's timeout_s.

claims.statement: build/Dockerfile and the toolbox's swath_go_build stage build the subject from the checksum-pinned source archive and the digest-pinned Go 1.27.4 builder.
claims.qualification: Toolbox images built from this recipe at 8c8f870 ran the attempts in benchmark/receipts/swath-go-main-8c8f870-cloud-20261111 and later receipts, which bind the image digests; no image digest is recorded inside this capsule.

evidence.reason: The image digests are bound in receipts outside this capsule's receipts/; the claim has not been re-evaluated against them.

claims.statement: The compiled argv runs under the benchmark worker, the dataset normalizes through the worker's dataset channel and the TSV files through its file channel.
claims.qualification: The adapter's argv ran against a scratch build of the subject over a synthetic local S3 store to make the adapter fixtures, and the normalizer reads those fixtures. Harness attempts at this pin are committed as diagnostic receipts under benchmark/receipts/.

evidence.reason: Harness attempts exist only as receipts outside this capsule's receipts/; the claim has not been re-evaluated against them.

claims.statement: A run against S3 lists every object in its scope exactly once.
claims.qualification: The coverage block is the tool's own claim of completeness and is not evidence of it. One live S3 run (real-changesets, earlier 7b05605 bundle) has a receipt under benchmark/receipts/; no reference manifest and no verifier verdict exist.

evidence.reason: No verifier verdict or reference manifest; the one live receipt is outside this capsule's receipts/ and from an earlier pin.

claims.statement: A run killed by SIGKILL and continued with swath resume commits a complete dataset holding each key once.
claims.qualification: Upstream documents the journal and a crash-matrix test suite; neither is a run of this study. Crash-resume is scale-dependent and is not settleable at smoke scale.

evidence.reason: No killed-and-resumed attempt has run; the harness's fault schedule is not on main.

claims.statement: Under real S3 throttling the limiter lowers the requests in flight below --workers and the run completes.
claims.qualification: The rules are source-established in claim limiter-is-aimd-on-throttle-answers; their behaviour against a throttling store is a run question.

evidence.reason: No run against a throttling store.

claims.statement: Wall clock, peak memory and spill at scale are within the bounds the run report, --sort-buffer and --spill-budget imply.
claims.qualification: --sort-buffer bounds rows held between listing and encoding, not the process; peak RSS is a run fact. Diagnostic wall clock and peak RSS at up to 143M objects are in receipts under benchmark/receipts/. Nothing here is comparative.

evidence.reason: The diagnostic receipts are outside this capsule's receipts/; the claim has not been re-evaluated against them.

claims.statement: Without --anonymous the port signs with the AWS SDK default credential chain the harness provides.
claims.qualification: The adapter drops --anonymous for a signed case; whether the harness's credential delivery reaches the SDK chain as the port expects is untested.

claims.statement: For the same bucket the Go port and the Java capsule's sorted Parquet mode produce the same key set and values.
claims.qualification: Receipts under benchmark/receipts/ hold one exact nine-column comparison (FourCast) and one probabilistic fingerprint plus order check of four products (blockchain), each against Java 0.3.2; neither covers every fixture.

evidence.reason: The comparisons are in receipts outside this capsule's receipts/; the claim has not been re-evaluated against them.

claims.statement: The study read the port's own public source and documentation, and the tool is built by the same organisation that runs the study.
claims.qualification: Only public files at the pinned revision were read; no Swath-internal material is used, and the port's measurements pages were not cited. The reading is recorded in research/derivation.md and the shared ownership in the repository's maintainer disclosure. This capsule was authored by one writer; one independent review was made of the a2efe16 capsule and its findings addressed, the move to 8c8f870 awaits its own independent review, and the owner's review is pending.
